message: Can you read this ECG for me?
reply:
My preliminary reading is **sinus bradycardia—a regular rhythm at about 50 beats/minute—with no obvious acute ischemic changes.** A clinician should confirm this using the original tracing and your symptoms.

- **Rhythm:** A P wave precedes each heartbeat; no obvious atrial fibrillation or skipped beats.
- **Axis and conduction:** Normal electrical axis. PR approximately 160 ms and QRS approximately 80–90 ms; no obvious heart block or bundle branch block.
- **QT:** Does not appear prolonged.
- **ST–T pattern:** Mild upward ST curvature in the chest leads may represent a normal repolarization variant. I don’t see convincing ST elevation suggesting an acute heart attack or significant reciprocal ST depression.

These measurements are estimates from the image. A slow sinus rhythm can be normal during rest or in fit people, but its significance depends on symptoms, medications, and previous ECGs.

**If you currently have chest pain, shortness of breath, fainting, or severe dizziness, seek emergency care now.** This image cannot rule out a heart attack. [Emergency warning signs](https://www.heart.org/en/news/2025/04/15/call-911-for-heart-attack-or-stroke-symptoms-or-just-drive-to-the-er)

How old are you, why was the ECG taken, and were you having any symptoms?
